title: Rejoiner rapid acculturation slate and rehiring rubric
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working slate captures a lightweight people-ops playbook for re-hiring former Redwood employees ("rejoiners"). The goal is: speed of reintegration + reduced context-switch friction + measured risk controls. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: quick screen rubric, offer cadence, 30/60/90 integration checkpoints, and a compact knowledge-transfer checklist for ICs and managers.

When to use this flow:
- Candidate is a previous Redwood employee who left voluntarily or via a structured program (not a global-termination).
- Return occurs within 12–36 months. For >36 months treat as external hire with elevated KT expectations.
- Applies to ICs, managers, and technical-lead roles. Executive rehires escalate to People Ops Director for case-by-case addenda.

Primary outcomes we measure:
- Time-to-first-meaningful-contribution (TTFMC) target: 30 days for ICs with prior same-team experience; 60 days otherwise.
- Access completion: 48 hours for core dev/tooling accesses; 72 hours for infra/admin.
- Knowledge debt flagged: list of 3 priority gaps and owner assigned by day 7.

Screening and rehiring rubric (interview-lite):
Purpose: quick validation of currency, role-fit, and re-onboarding risk. Use when candidate has >6 months prior Redwood tenure.
Interview components (one 45–60m loop usually sufficient):
- People Ops touch (30m): discuss reason for return, expectations, manager-of-record, compensation anchors, and open HR items (non-competes, waivers). Score categories: clarity of motivation, cultural fit, unresolved concerns.
- Technical/role fit (45–60m): manager or peer-level technical check focused on current role’s responsibilities. Score: technical currency, system knowledge, and ramp timeline realism.
- Team sync (30m, optional): quick chat with 1–2 future peers to validate day-to-day fit and cultural dynamics.

Rubric scales (0–3 each, note examples):
- Motivation clarity (0: unclear/contradictory, 1: ambiguous, 2: plausible, 3: mission-aligned + constructive reasons)
- Risk of knowledge drift (0: significant risk, 1: moderate, 2: small, 3: negligible)
- Role capability match (0: mismatch, 1: gaps requiring >3 months ramp, 2: modest ramp, 3: immediate contributor)
- Manager confidence (0: do not rehire, 1: rehire with probation, 2: rehire, 3: rehire + stretch remit)

Decision thresholds (suggested):
- Sum >= 9: proceed with standard rehire offer.
- Sum 6–8: proceed with targeted probation (60–90d) and defined KT plan.
- Sum <=5: decline or convert to external hire with extended onboarding.

Compensation and offer cadence notes:
- Default approach: match internal market benchmark for role and tenure; prioritize keep-it-simple packages for rehires to speed acceptance.
- Equity: evaluate remaining previous equity (if applicable) and follow standard RSU regrant policy; escalate anomalies to compensation team.
- Offer timeline target: verbal within 48 hours of final loop, written within 96 hours.

Pre-boarding checklist (to complete between verbal offer acceptance and first day):
- Assign buddy and manager: People Ops assigns a buddy from same squad; manager confirms first-7-days calendar.
- Access matrix: engineering accounts, repo access, Slack, corp Google, CI tokens — ticket created to infra with 48h SLA.
- Prior artifacts handoff: request previous repos/PRs, design docs, and postmortems from candidate’s tenure. Candidate to list top 5 ownership areas before start.
- Compliance clearance: ensure exit paperwork from previous stint is reviewed; confirm no outstanding IP/NDAs conflicts.

Day 0–7: rapid acculturation checklist
Manager responsibilities:
- Day 0 intro: 30m welcome + core expectations + OKR alignment for first 30 days.
- Day 2 1:1: set 3 deliverables for 30d and identify two learning targets.
- Assign KT owner(s): one peer + one manager to own knowledge transfer topics.

Buddy responsibilities:
- Share team rituals, channel etiquette, common engineering patterns, and 'where things live' doc.
- Walkthrough of local dev environment and quickstart repo (goal: run tests locally within 48 hours).

Technical KT checklist (for engineers):
- Repo mapping: list of repos to re-familiarize with and a single issue or PR to review each.
- Infra access and sandboxes: ensure staging creds and test harnesses available by day 2.
- Runbook review: review 3 oncall/runbook entries relevant to prior ownership.
- Regression checkpoint: pair on a small bug fix by day 7 (owner: buddy/peer).

Culture & product catch-up:
- Send product one-pager and 3 recent roadmap changes before start.
- Schedule a 45m product update with PM within first week.
- Invite to two recurring team rituals by day 3.

30/60/90 milestone template (manager fill-in):
- 30d: list measurable outputs (e.g., merged feature X or ownership of incident runbook). Confirm access parity.
- 60d: independent ownership of a scope slice; maintain sprint velocity.
- 90d: fully onboarded to original level OR agreed new role; 1:1 skip-level check-in scheduled.

Probation notes and remediation flow: 
- For rehired contributors assigned probation, set explicit success criteria at offer stage and include scheduled mid-probation review.
- Failure to meet probation triggers 'remediate -> documented plan -> final review' cascade; People Ops and manager co-own.

Knowledge-transfer template items (quick fields for manager to track):
- Previous ownership artifacts (list), current gaps (top 3), assigned KT partners (names), KT due dates.

Manager/People Ops coordination checklist (pre-start and week 1):
- Confirm payroll reactivation and benefits re-enrollment window.
- Confirm return-to-office flex profile (if local policy changed).
- Re-invite to security trainings and compliance modules (if lapsed >12 months).

Red flags and extra diligence triggers:
- Candidate left due to documented performance issues: escalate to People Ops for deeper review and reference checks.
- Non-compete or legal entanglements: require legal sign-off.
- Candidate requests materially different role with manager not aligned: pause and re-align expectations.

Communication templates (short samples)
- Offer: one-paragraph verbal template and an email template that includes probation and 30/60/90 expectations. Keep terse, clear, and time-boxed.
- Manager welcome note: 3 bullets — first deliverable, buddy contact, and one quick win.

Open questions / TODOs (working items to finalize this slate):
- Should we standardize a 30% expedited access pipeline for rehires with >12 months prior tenure? (ops input needed)
- Determine equity regrant cadence for rehired engineers who previously received RSUs. (comp team)
- Build a small Confluence template for manager KT tracking (owner: Marco).

Appendix: sample 30-day deliverable template (manager to paste into offer)
- Week 1: onboard, run local tests, pair on current sprint bug.
- Week 2: deliver a small scoped PR with tests and docs.
- Week 3: shadow production deploy and lead a rollback runbook dry-run.
- Week 4: present a short retro on knowledge gaps and propose next 30-day objectives.

Notes to self / authoring log:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel 2025-09-12. Iterated with Marco and Sofia 2025-09-25. Revised for probation language and comp notes 2025-10-02.

Quick links (for manager):
- Rehire offer checklist (internal doc): confluence:REHIRE-CHK
- Infra access ticket template: https://infra.redwood.ai/templates/access-rehire

End of slate. This is a working document — comment directly in doc, flag missing items with [ACTION], and tag People Ops for approvals before publishing as canonical rehire playbook.
